summary.tagline: Traverse the stairways of the bog to reach high-altitude limestone vistas.
summary.seo_title: Visiting Marble Arch Caves and Cuilcagh Boardwalk

travel.headline: Advance parking reservations for the Cuilcagh Boardwalk
travel.reservation: Access to the primary boardwalk parking area requires a pre-booking system via a private operator. While the nature reserve parking is free, availability is limited and fills quickly. Always verify the current status of the visitor centre and trail access before travel.

days.title: Cuilcagh Mountain Wilderness

stops.name: Cuilcagh Boardwalk Trail
stops.detail: Hike through one of the largest blanket bogs in Northern Ireland toward a steep wooden staircase built to protect the fragile habitat.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes to reach Marlbank Road; conditions vary on narrow local lanes.
days.note: Stay within the viewing platform at the top as the summit habitat is fragile; dogs are strictly prohibited.

intel.title: Restricted Trailhead Parking
intel.text: The main trailhead lot is privately owned and operates on a pre-booking system at theboardwalk.ie. Killykeeghan Nature Reserve offers alternative free parking a short distance further along the road.

intel.title: Mobile Coverage Gaps
intel.text: Mobile reception in the Cuilcagh Mountain area is generally poor. Inform a contact of your expected return time and carry a physical map and compass for navigation.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Fuel and primary supplies should be secured in Enniskillen before turning onto the rural A32 and Marlbank roads. There are no refueling facilities within the immediate geopark trailheads.

intel.title: Variable Peak Traffic
intel.text: While the walk typically takes three hours, busy days can see significant congestion extending the visit time. Check local social media for real-time updates on visitor volume.

intel.title: Mountain Terrain Hazards
intel.text: Weather on the mountain changes rapidly and can become inhospitable year-round. The trail includes steep stairwells and boulder fields that are not wheelchair accessible.

plan.arrival: Pick up a rental vehicle in Enniskillen and follow the A4 Sligo Road toward the A32 Swanlinbar Road. Check into local accommodation before proceeding to the narrow Marlbank Road trailheads.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for the paved Marlbank Road, though lanes are narrow; check RV width restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: The Cuilcagh viewing platform provides expansive views of the lowlands during the late afternoon light, though hikers should descend before dusk due to visibility concerns.
